claims.text: Replacing conventional EAM references with a machine-learning potential trained on ab initio liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The machine-learning reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed intervention is to train the machine-learning potential on ab initio configurations with emphasis on liquid-state data.
The proposed temperature range is approximately 0.9–1.1 times the alloy melting temperature.
The proposed method applies to alloys having at least five or near-equiatomic principal elements.
A liquid-trained machine-learning potential can capture a greater diversity of atomic configurations and complex liquid-phase interactions than a conventional EAM reference.
Training on a diverse set of ab initio configurations makes the machine-learning potential reproduce the ab initio potential-energy surface more accurately.
More accurate reproduction of the potential-energy surface improves phase-space overlap between the reference and ab initio target systems.
Improved phase-space overlap reduces discontinuities or mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path.
Traditional EAM references exhibit thermodynamic-integration-path discontinuities for the systems under consideration.
Reducing thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will yield more accurate free-energy estimates.
The improvement should be significant relative to the EAM baseline, although its exact magnitude is uncertain.
TOR-TILD calculations using EAM references provide the proposed baseline.
The method is primarily applicable to high-entropy-alloy compositions represented in the machine-learning training set.
Performance may diminish for compositions or temperatures not adequately covered by the ab initio training data.
A reduction of less than approximately 10% in both path mismatch and free-energy estimation error is proposed as a falsification threshold.
